The Case

We only get one year. Let's get more out of it.

Students naturally get to know the people they sit beside, work with, or meet early on. In a one-year program, it's easy to spend most of it inside the same few circles.

The goal isn't simply more events. It's to create more reasons for people across the MScA to meet, participate, and build real relationships over the year.

The Plan

Four things I'd actually work on.

  1. Get the clubs what they need

    Every MScA club should have the support to actually get events and initiatives off the ground, from funding to logistics to a straight answer when they're stuck. Unblocking that is a big part of what a Co-President is there to do.

  2. A clear person to go to

    Everyone should feel comfortable knowing exactly who to reach out to when they need help with anything, whether that's academic, social, or something else. No guessing, and no falling through the cracks.

  3. Listen more than we announce

    Better communication starts with hearing you. That means the MScA checking in often, through surveys and in person, so we actually know what students want instead of assuming.

  4. More hands, more momentum

    Where it helps, create more MScA positions so projects and initiatives keep real momentum, instead of stalling on one or two overloaded people.

The Evidence

This isn't my first time doing the work.

Exhibit C

Co-founder and VP of a club in undergrad

Built a club from scratch and ran it as VP, hosting large-scale events and raising a real amount of money for local charities. It only worked through delegation, building and managing teams to actually get things done.

Exhibit D

Fundraising in the community

Kept it going beyond school, raising money for charities through running and other events. Showing up for the people around me isn't a campaign line. It's a habit.
